title: Desk Guidance on the Rolling 12-Month Night Limit for Respite and Short Stays
content:
Respite and short stays under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement are aggregated across all of a customer's stays. The nights counted for the customer in the rolling 12 months ending on the planned departure date, including the nights now requested, may not exceed the night limit per rolling 12 months of the stay type being booked or extended. A booking or extension that would exceed the annual limit is refused for the nights beyond it; a guest who needs longer care is directed to a permanent residency admission instead of another short stay. Nights of cancelled stays never count, and nights of a converted stay count up to the conversion.

## What is counted

The window is the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the planned departure date of the stay being booked or extended, each night counted by its date. Within that window the count is:

- the nights of the customer's stays in in-stay, completed or converted status that fall in the window;
- plus the booked nights of the customer's other stays in booked status;
- plus the nights of the stay being booked or extended.

The count is taken from the company's stay records (check-in and check-out dates and stay status) for that customer, before the booking or extension is recorded. The limit compared against is the one of the stay type being booked or extended, not the type of an earlier stay.

## Applies to

| Request | Checked against the limit |
|---|---|
| Booking a new stay | Yes |
| Extending a stay | Yes |

## Status of earlier stays

| Status of an earlier stay | Its nights in the count |
|---|---|
| In stay, completed | Nights falling in the window |
| Converted | Nights up to the conversion, falling in the window |
| Booked (another stay) | Its booked nights |
| Cancelled | Never counted |

## Worked count (hypothetical customer)

A hypothetical customer asks to book an Assisted Living Respite Stay (Standard Care), whose limit is the 90 nights shown on the stay type's schedule, for 20 nights. Within the 365 days ending on the planned departure date the customer has a completed stay of 50 nights and a cancelled stay of 14 nights. The count is 50 plus 20, that is 70 nights; the cancelled nights do not count. 70 does not exceed 90, so the annual limit does not stand in the way.

Had the same customer asked for 45 nights, the count would be 50 plus 45, that is 95 nights, 5 nights beyond the limit; the request is refused for those 5 nights beyond it.
